cards.headline:
Kimi's K3.1 agents now work
inside Unity, Unreal and Blender
cards.body: Moonshot's Kimi agents edit engine projects directly, and one 20-hour unattended run recreated an existing game.

blocks.x: Moonshot AI has released a game development and creative work solution for Kimi, built on its Kimi K3.1 model series, its Kimi Code and Kimi Work agent products, and plugins for professional tools including Unity, Unreal Engine and Blender. The company says it is meant to help studios test gameplay ideas sooner and move engineering and art production forward.

The model reads design documents, screenshots, code and 3D assets and plans the work; Kimi Code handles implementation inside a codebase, while Kimi Work takes on multi-step production tasks. In Unity and Unreal Engine, it maps the code structure, scene hierarchy and module dependencies, makes changes through editor plugins, and checks the result against reproduction steps, logs and runtime data.

For Unity, Kimi works with Tuanjie Codely Agent from Unity China. In one demonstration, Kimi says, it worked for 20 hours without human intervention, recreating an existing game and producing a native project that can be developed further.

Showcase builds credited to Kimi K3.1 Pro include a Blender rainforest valley flythrough and, in Unreal Engine 5.8, a celestial palace scene totaling 36 million triangles. Kimi also says designers without coding experience can produce playable Godot prototypes in one to two days.
